_purpose: Per-stroke brush prompts for A1's eight eye-level stroke cameras, in the shape brush_cloud_step.py requires: a prompt string per --key, plus _negative, plus _order. Consumed by `brush_cloud_step.py graph --prompts <this file>` (Stage 1, out of this arc's scope -- this file is authored so Stage 1 can start without a round trip, per this repo's own rule that a spec nobody can start is a shelf).
_convention_followed_and_why_MECHANICAL_: IDENTICAL full-coverage prompt on all 8 keys, matching E58-a1-twin-prompts.json's convention -- NOT W3's actual brush convention (E08-brush-prompts.json), which appends a per-view ORIENTATION phrase ('seen from the front' / 'in profile' / 'seen from behind, at three-quarters' / 'seen from directly behind') on top of an already-full, view-unfiltered spec. The reason is not a style preference: `brush_cloud_step.py graph`'s only canon_gate call (`canon_gate.require_canon(P[args.key], canon_path=..., subject=..., no_canon=..., profile_path=...)`, no `scope=` kwarg) runs at the DEFAULT scope, which is `scope="subject"`. At subject scope canon_gate.py's `unlicensed_residue()` refuses ANY prompt text that is not built entirely from this subject's own licensed spans (occupant phrases + legal_clauses + blocked_additions + joint phrases) -- and `canon/a1.surfaces.json` licenses NO orientation-class legal_clause (only framing/style/staging classes exist, none of them an orientation phrase). Adding W3-style orientation phrases here would therefore be UNLICENSED RESIDUE and would refuse at `graph` time. Editing canon to license one is explicitly out of this arc's authority (the Director ratifies canon). Verified directly, not assumed: `E:\AI\training\facet_E72\scripts\verify_prompt.py` against the live `canon_gate.py` -- at scope=subject the composed string below returns ok=True, missing=[], forbidden=[], unlicensed=[], out_of_scope=[] (console: `E:\AI\training\facet_E72\logs\step6_verify_prompt_console.txt`).
_the_scope_tension_named_not_resolved: The SAME verification script also checked this identical string at PER-VIEW scope (scope="view:0".."view:7") purely informationally -- brush_cloud_step.py does not use scope="view:*" anywhere today, so this is not what actually gates Stage 1. Result: views 0/1/2/7 (the full-face-set views) pass; views 3/4/5 (out_of_scope=3 each -- face/eyes/mouth, dropped from those scopes.views entries) and view 6 (out_of_scope=2 -- eyes/mouth, per the Director's E66 ruling on that one view) FAIL a per-view gate that nothing currently applies. This is a real, disclosed tension between what `scopes.views` says a camera can see and what the actual brush prompt says on every stroke -- named here rather than silently resolved, since resolving it either way (wiring brush_cloud_step.py to scope="stroke:X", or accepting the mismatch permanently) is a design decision this arc does not make.
_composed_from: The CURRENT 19-phrase ratified string already sitting in profiles/a1.json's tools."restylize_views.py".prompt field (E58 Stage B/D; amended E59 Stage 0 +stage_head_forward; amended 2026-08-18 +stage_arms/+stage_hands/+stage_feet; N1 gained SLEEVELESS at E60) -- reused verbatim rather than retyped, so there is exactly one place this string is authored and this file quotes it. This is the file's post-E59/E60 successor to E58-a1-twin-prompts.json's OWN 18-phrase (pre-stage_head_forward) string; the same _rule_deviation_disclosed reasoning that file gave for full, unfiltered, identical-per-view coverage applies again here, now for an independent, mechanical reason (the canon-gate wiring above) rather than only the charter's original instruction.

Deliberate, not a default: matching ship.json's own precedent for a subject with no prior brush strokes ('No stroke has run here, so this subject has earned no brush-stage terms yet; when it does they are added the way W3's were, with the measurement') -- W3's brush negative adds belt-failure terms MEASURED at the brush stage specifically on that character; A1 has no such measurement yet, so nothing is invented here. When stroke 1 runs and returns something, any measured A1-specific brush failure terms get added the way W3's were, not before.
